from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors are directed arrows with magnitude.", "Vector addition moves an end effector.", "Scalar multiplication stretches or flips vectors."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Geometry of Vectors", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B4", "E6")
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        v = Vector([3, 2], color=WHITE)
        v.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - v.get_start())
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v} = (3, 2)", color="#FF8C00").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A5")
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        u = Vector([1, 1], color=BLUE)
        u.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - u.get_start())
        v_offset = Vector([3, 2], color=WHITE)
        v_offset.shift(axes.c2p(1, 1) - v_offset.get_start())
        sum_vec = Vector([4, 3], color=GREEN)
        sum_vec.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - sum_vec.get_start())
        
        self.play(Create(u), Create(v_offset))
        self.play(Create(sum_vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        c = ValueTracker(1.0)
        v_scaled = always_redraw(lambda: Vector([3*c.get_value(), 2*c.get_value()], color=RED).shift(axes.c2p(0,0)))
        
        self.play(FadeOut(u), FadeOut(v_offset), FadeOut(sum_vec), FadeOut(v))
        self.add(v_scaled)
        self.play(c.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=2)
        self.play(c.animate.set_value(-0.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear combinations combine vectors: c1v1 plus c2v2.",
            "Span is the set of all reachable points.",
            "Varying coefficients covers the entire plane."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations and Span", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animation Elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        v1 = Vector([1, 0.5], color=WHITE)
        v2 = Vector([0, 1], color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        v1_label = MathTex("v_1").next_to(v1.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        v2_label = MathTex("v_2").next_to(v2.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2), Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")
        
        # Parallelogram for v1 + v2
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            ORIGIN, v1.get_end(), v1.get_end() + v2.get_end(), v2.get_end(),
            color="#00CED1", fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        v1_plus_v2 = Vector(v1.get_end() + v2.get_end(), color="#00CED1")
        v1_plus_v2_label = MathTex("v_1 + v_2", color="#00CED1").next_to(v1_plus_v2.get_end(), UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(parallelogram), Create(v1_plus_v2), Write(v1_plus_v2_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Grid/Span visualization
        span_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 3):
            for j in range(-2, 3):
                point = i * v1.get_end() + j * v2.get_end()
                dot = Dot(point, color="#FFFF00", radius=0.05)
                span_grid.add(dot)
                
        self.play(FadeIn(span_grid))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector", [
            "Linear dependence occurs with redundant vectors.",
            "One vector as a combination of others.",
            "Redundant vectors add no new directional coverage."
        ])
        
        # Define vectors
        origin = np.array([0, 0, 0])
        v1 = Arrow(start=self.grid['D3'], end=self.grid['B3'], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Arrow(start=self.grid['D3'], end=self.grid['D5'], color=GREEN)
        v3 = Arrow(start=self.grid['D3'], end=self.grid['B5'], color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), Create(v1), Create(v2), Create(v3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show v3 = v1 + v2 relationship

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE), Indicate(v3))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Bases: The Minimal Blueprint", [
            "A basis is both linearly independent and spans.",
            "It is the minimal set of vectors.",
            "Bases describe every point in space uniquely."
        ])

        # Define vectors
        b1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE)
        b2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=WHITE)
        l1 = MathTex("b_1", color=WHITE).next_to(b1.get_end(), DOWN)
        l2 = MathTex("b_2", color=WHITE).next_to(b2.get_end(), LEFT)
        basis_group = VGroup(b1, b2, l1, l2)
        
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.0 + UP*1.0, color=YELLOW)
        lv = MathTex("v", color=YELLOW).next_to(v.get_end(), RIGHT)
        
        basis_label = Text("Basis", color="#32CD32")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.place_in_area(basis_group, "A1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(basis_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.place_at_grid(v, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(lv, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(GrowArrow(v), Write(lv))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.place_at_grid(basis_label, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(basis_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Span defines the reach of your system.",
            "Linear independence prevents all redundant information.",
            "Basis provides the most efficient coordinate description."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements
        # B035: Unified visual model
        triangle = Polygon(LEFT+DOWN, RIGHT+DOWN, UP, color=BLUE).scale(1.2)
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("Span", font_size=20),
            Text("Indep.", font_size=20),
            Text("Basis", font_size=20)
        )
        labels[0].next_to(triangle.get_vertices()[2], UP)
        labels[1].next_to(triangle.get_vertices()[0], LEFT)
        labels[2].next_to(triangle.get_vertices()[1], RIGHT)
        
        system = VGroup(triangle, labels)
        self.place_in_area(system, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(system))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Indicate(triangle))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Rotate(triangle, angle=PI/3, about_point=triangle.get_center()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        final_text = Text("Basis = Efficiency", color=GOLD).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "F3")
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vector Spaces: Span, Dependence, and Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Geometry of Vectors
sections.content: Briefly define a vector as an arrow in 2D space with magnitude and direction. Explain vector addition and scalar multiplication as 'stretching' or 'flipping' vectors.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Robot Arm' in 2D; moving the end effector by combining two base motor vectors.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Define linear combination: c1v1 + c2v2. Introduce 'Span' as the set of all reachable points. Use a graphic showing a 2D plane being 'filled' by varying the coefficients of two non-parallel vectors.
sections.example: A drone moving in 2D space. If you have two vectors (forward-left and forward-right), you can reach any point on the ground (Span = 2D plane).

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector
sections.content: Explain linear dependence as having a 'redundant' vector. If one vector is a scalar multiple of another (or a combo of others), it adds no new directional coverage.
sections.example: Three hikers walking in a line. If the third hiker is just following the first two, the 'span' of their movement doesn't expand; they are linearly dependent.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimal Blueprint
sections.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that are linearly independent AND span the entire space. It is the 'minimal set' needed to describe every point uniquely.
sections.example: Standard Cartesian coordinates (i, j). Using only two vectors to describe every point on a map uniquely; removing one makes it impossible to reach the whole space.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Synthesize the logic: Span covers the space, Linear Independence ensures no redundancy, and Basis provides the most efficient coordinate system.
sections.example: 3D Gaming Engine: Using a basis of (x, y, z) vectors to locate every pixel on a 3D character model efficiently.
